comment: Seccomp profile for the assistant-claude service. Unlike the three Go services (gateway/mcp/validator), this container runs the official Claude Code CLI, a Node.js program whose runtime needs a large, moving syscall set (TTY ioctls, clone3, io_uring probes, memfd, epoll/eventfd variants). A hand-maintained ERRNO allowlist would crash-loop the moment Node reached for a syscall we forgot, so this profile is allow-by-default with a denylist of the escape-relevant syscalls instead. It is defense-in-depth on top of the container's stronger controls (cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read_only root, non-root uid 1000, pids/mem/cpu limits, and network isolation), which already neuter the capability-gated syscalls. Denied syscalls return ENOSYS (38) rather than EPERM so any runtime fallback path (e.g. libuv's io_uring probe) engages cleanly.

syscalls.comment: Mounting, namespace pivoting and the new fs* mount API — hand back the container-escape power that cap_drop already denies; refused here by name so nothing can re-enable them by accident.
Kernel module and kexec surface — never used by Node; loading code into the kernel is a direct escape.
Process tracing / cross-process memory — Node never traces; ptrace and process_vm_* would let this container read or steer neighbouring processes.
eBPF, perf and kernel keyring — broad kernel attack surface unrelated to running a chat CLI.
Host-wide time, accounting, swap and legacy priv syscalls — not needed by an unprivileged application container.
